name: Lamassu
description: The Lamassu is a Mesopotamian protective deity depicted as a colossal hybrid figure with a human head, the body of a bull or lion and the wings of an eagle. Monumental Assyrian lamassu pairs were placed at city and palace gates from the Neo-Assyrian period.

aliases.name: Lamma
aliases.meaning: early-period name of the protective female deity

aliases.name: Aladlammû
aliases.meaning: winged-bull / guardian spirit, used interchangeably with lamassu in Assyrian contexts

origin: Originally an artistic and religious tradition of southern Mesopotamia (Sumer / Akkad); reaches its monumental culmination in the Neo-Assyrian Empire of the 9th–7th centuries BC, with examples from Nimrud, Khorsabad and Nineveh in present-day Iraq. The form was subsequently absorbed by the Achaemenid Persian Empire (Persepolis).
